review_output: {"summary":"I re-checked the earlier MAJOR credential-race finding against the actual claim guard, and that race no longer applies. The claim reads the account again inside the same Serializable transaction and checks its status and accountVersion before the draft compare-and-swap. If a credential save commits first, that check fails and the result is \"conflict\". If the claim commits first, the credential save sees status \"syncing\" and is blocked. If both overlap, each transaction reads the row the other one writes, so PostgreSQL's serializable isolation aborts one of them. This holds as long as both transactions really run at Serializable on PostgreSQL, which the actual-PG interleaving test covers. The 2mb body limit, the 1,000,000-byte image cap, the sync_failed mapping with revalidation, and the conflict guards on revision all look sound for the stated budget. Two MINOR issues remain, both about getting stuck or seeing an unhelpful error.
